notes: DISCOVERY RETROFIT (leviathan-e4-wt lane): the scheduled biweekly fetch previously ran fetch_unica_biweekly.py with NO args -- a manifest-only download (no --discover), so genuinely new bulletins (the entire 2026/27 season) never entered the manifest and the fetch was a green no-op forever. Fixed: the biweekly fetch now runs --discover --current-season --asof <scheduled-time>. --current-season derives the open Centre-South harvest season (YYYY/YYYY+1, April-crush labelling) from the scheduler asof via fetch_unica_biweekly.current_harvest_season(), scoping the LIVE JS-portal Playwright discovery + the download to that single season; it auto-advances at the April boundary (no hardcoded year to go stale). NEEDS Playwright/chromium in the Batch image (docker/leviathan_worker/Dockerfile now installs .[batch,biweekly] + playwright install --with-deps chromium; main loop rebuilds). No-op-green gap (fetch _exit_reason returns None on uploaded=0 skipped>0) left AS-IS deliberately -- quiet fortnights must not go red; the poller lane owns staleness detection. Annual/state producer is CLASS-A (shadow_canonical, named jobdef); biweekly producer is CLASS-B latest_only (held until A-W4) -- so the family stays held (promote_mode=stop_and_notify, retrofit_landed=false; silver publishes --publish-mode shadow, promote.tasks EMPTY -- shadow-only soak per the futures_prices precedent; canonical promotion is a main-loop KMS-signed manual leg). retrofit_landed stays FALSE: test_wave2_is_exactly_the_classb_set binds unica to the retrofit_required-and-not-landed set, and the SFN [Promote] Map runs promote.tasks on a GREEN gate regardless of promote.mode -- so populating promote IS the autonomous arm and is gated on the user's go. Fortnight iteration. silver_unica_corn_ethanol + silver_unica_monthly_ethanol_sales have no direct producer (derived) and are out of this chain's gate. D-SG G2-1(a) 2026-08-16: (1) the biweekly silver leg now carries an EXPLICIT --publish-mode shadow. It is publish_mode=latest_only, and gen_sfn_inputs._render_task appends --publish-mode ONLY to shadow_canonical publishers -- so its bare command rendered bare and unica_biweekly_silver_task.py:110 defaulted to dry-run: three biweekly tables were never written by the schedule in ANY mode (08-12 log: 'mode=dry-run'). Same class as the fgis 07-23 bare-command fix, same remedy. (2) The annual leg stays BARE ON PURPOSE: it is shadow_canonical, so the renderer supplies --publish-mode shadow (verified in the live tfvars payload). Adding it to the descriptor would render the flag TWICE. spec_noops edit a14 called this descriptor 'stale vs live' -- it is not; the divergence is the renderer's publish-stage contract. (3) --through-current-season was ADDED then ROLLED BACK the same day: the M-8 probe (2026-08-16, run through the fetcher's own request path) confirmed the May-2026 note -- seasons 2021/2022..2026/2027 return EMPTY TABLE SHELLS (a <table> tag, exactly 4 header <tr>, no data; 2020/2021 real page = 28 <tr>) that PASSED the fetcher's size+<table> bar, so the flag would have uploaded six garbage shells weekly. The endpoint's data ceiling is 2020/2021; the biweekly leg IS the current-season source. The flag stays in code (tested) for the day the portal serves data; fetch_unica._assert_data_rows now REFUSES shells so that day announces itself as a fence trip, never a silent upload. silver_unica_annual_state is therefore STATIC at the endpoint ceiling (G5 census class), not stale. (4) The deliberate 'quiet fortnights must not go red' no-op-green gap is now NARROWED, not removed: fetch_unica_biweekly._exit_reason fails only when the run is season-scoped AND the open season is >45 days past 1 April AND the manifest holds ZERO bulletins for it. A quiet fortnight still shows skipped>0 and stays green.
